extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff, and legal professionals subject to USPTO disciplinary processes
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO OED order imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion from practice before the USPTO) based on a state court disbarment, describing procedural steps, publication, account restrictions, and the regulatory authorities and duties that apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a state's duly constituted authority (here, the June 30, 2021 Order of the New York Appellate Division), pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director filed a Complaint requesting reciprocal discipline and sent a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' notifying Respondent and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If Respondent fails to file a response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory violation cited: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline is predicated upon violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), which is triggered by being disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the exclusion is for violating § 11.804(h), predicated upon the respondent's disbarment in New York.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion is the substantive discipline ordered. The order explicitly states the respondent 'is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements (Notice & Order and response period)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order' must be served (here, sent by certified mail) notifying the respondent of the Complaint and providing an opportunity to respond within a specified period (40 days). If notice cannot be delivered, it shall be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Notice and Order was sent by certified mail; when it could not be delivered it was published in the Official Gazette (dates given). The Notice provided 40 days to oppose on grounds enumerated in § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs publication at https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/ and requires an Official Gazette notice 'materially consistent' with the provided template. It also states disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template content for Official Gazette notice of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must identify the respondent (name, city, registration number), summarize the reciprocal disciplinary action, cite the regulatory violation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and summarize the basis (state disbarment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes a model 'Notice of Exclusion' that names the respondent, gives the registration number, states the discipline (excluded from practice before USPTO), cites § 11.804(h), summarizes the state proceedings (including suspension, charges, and disbarment), and references 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the authorities for the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to other disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifically directs the OED Director to give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to relevant agencies and courts and to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of disciplined practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the final order does not restate § 11.58, it mandates compliance with those duties (which govern obligations such as client notification, file transfer/retention, and trust account handling for attorneys who are suspended or disbarred).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO.gov account disabling and suspension authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to the respondent (including any accounts respondent established, sponsored, or used in connection with any matter before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order authorizes disabling/suspending accounts 'as of the date of this Final Order' and notes USPTO need not re-activate any such account sua sponte; re-activation is respondent's responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on obtaining or using USPTO verified Electronic System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Until reinstatement, respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have his name added to any USPTO verified Electronic System account, and is prohibited from using, assessing, or assisting others in using/accessing any USPTO.gov accounts or other USPTO filing systems for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order enumerates specific prohibitions: (1) opening/activating accounts for preparing/filing, (2) applying for accounts for preparing/filing, (3) verifying or attempting to verify any other person's credentials for such accounts, and (4) sponsoring or attempting to sponsor accounts for preparing/filing. These prohibitions remain until a reinstatement petition under § 11.60 is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement governed by 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition seeking reinstatement to practice before the USPTO must be granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states that until a petition seeking reinstatement is granted under § 11.60, the prohibitions and account restrictions remain in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying grounds from state discipline deemed established
rubrics_metrics.description: State charges that were deemed established (by the New York Appellate Division's June 30, 2021 Order) included misappropriation of funds entrusted as a fiduciary, cash withdrawals from attorney special account, failure to render an account, failure to maintain required bank and bookkeeping records, failure to cooperate with the Grievance Committee, conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice, and conduct adversely reflecting on fitness as a lawyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice and the Final Order summarize the state proceedings and list the specific misconduct allegations that supported the state court's disbarment. The state court deemed the verified petition's charges established after respondent neither served nor filed an answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutes/regulations as the legal basis for imposing reciprocal discipline and making disciplinary decisions publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certification of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Order must be served on the respondent at the most recent address provided to OED and on counsel for the OED Director; certificate of service documents the means (certified mail, email), addresses, and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document concludes with a Certificate of Service describing first-class certified mail to respondent and email to OED counsel, as required procedural step for final orders.
